\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حالت} (hālat)}{حالت (hālat)}]{\ur{حالت} (hālat) — a state (of health, of repair)}

\label{lesson:UR-C365-halat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for prominent, then the Urdu for to emerge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حالت}}
\textbf{\ur{حالت}} — \emph{hālat} — \textquotedblleft{}a state (of health, of repair)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{مریض} \ur{کی} \ur{حالت} \ur{ٹھیک} \ur{نہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{ہسپتال} \ur{لے} \ur{جائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar marīz kī hālat ṭhīk nahīṅ to haspatāl le jāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the patient is not well, take him to hospital.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حالت}} (\emph{hālat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥāla}, \textquotedblleft{}a state, a condition\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar marīz kī hālat ṭhīk nahīṅ to haspatāl le jāiye.} — If the patient is not well, take him to hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for prominent, then the Urdu for to emerge, then say \emph{hālat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{حالت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A state (of health, of repair)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{صورت} \ur{حال} (sūrat-e-hāl)}{صورت حال (sūrat-e-hāl)}]{\ur{صورت} \ur{حال} (sūrat-e-hāl) — a situation}

\label{lesson:UR-C365-surat-e-hal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to emerge, then the Urdu for a state.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{صورت} \ur{حال}}
\textbf{\ur{صورت} \ur{حال}} — \emph{sūrat-e-hāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a situation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{صورت} \ur{حال} \ur{بدلی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{بھی} \ur{بدلیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sūrat-e-hāl badlī to ham bhī badleṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the situation changes, we will change too.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{صورت} \ur{حال}} (\emph{sūrat-e-hāl}) is built from two loans, each usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic: Arabic \emph{ṣūra}, \textquotedblleft{}a form\textquotedblright{}, and Arabic \emph{ḥāl}, \textquotedblleft{}a state\textquotedblright{}. The shape things are in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūrat-e-hāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūrat-e-hāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar sūrat-e-hāl badlī to ham bhī badleṅ ge.} — If the situation changes, we will change too.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to emerge, then the Urdu for a state, then say \emph{sūrat-e-hāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{صورت} \ur{حال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A situation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مصیبت} (musībat)}{مصیبت (musībat)}]{\ur{مصیبت} (musībat) — a hardship; trouble}

\label{lesson:UR-C365-musibat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a state, then the Urdu for a situation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مصیبت}}
\textbf{\ur{مصیبت}} — \emph{musībat} — \textquotedblleft{}a hardship; trouble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{رک} \ur{گئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{مصیبت} \ur{میں} \ur{ہوں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar gāṛī ruk gaī to ham musībat meṅ hoṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the car breaks down, we will be in trouble.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مصیبت}} (\emph{musībat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muṣība}, \textquotedblleft{}a misfortune\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a state, then the Urdu for a situation, then say \emph{musībat} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تبدیلی} (tabdīlī)}{تبدیلی (tabdīlī)}]{\ur{تبدیلی} (tabdīlī) — a change}

\label{lesson:UR-C365-tabdili}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a situation, then the Urdu for a hardship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تبدیلی}}
\textbf{\ur{تبدیلی}} — \emph{tabdīlī} — \textquotedblleft{}a change\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{قانون} \ur{میں} \ur{تبدیلی} \ur{آئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ٹیکس} \ur{کم} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar qānūn meṅ tabdīlī āī to ṭaiks kam ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the law changes, the tax will come down.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تبدیلی}} (\emph{tabdīlī}) is built on \emph{tabdīl}, \textquotedblleft{}changing\textquotedblright{}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tabdīl}, with the noun ending \emph{-ī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar qānūn meṅ tabdīlī āī to ṭaiks kam ho gā.} — If the law changes, the tax will come down.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a situation, then the Urdu for a hardship, then say \emph{tabdīlī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھنسانا} (phansānā)}{پھنسانا (phansānā)}]{\ur{پھنسانا} (phansānā) — to land in trouble; to trap}

\label{lesson:UR-C365-phansana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a hardship, then the Urdu for a change.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھنسانا}}
\textbf{\ur{پھنسانا}} — \emph{phansānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to land in trouble; to trap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{نے} \ur{جھوٹ} \ur{کہا} \ur{تو} \ur{مجھے} \ur{بھی} \ur{پھنساؤ} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum ne jhūṭ kahā to mujhe bhī phansāo ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you tell a lie, you will drag me into trouble too.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{پھنسایا}, \emph{us ne mujhe phansāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پھنسانا}} (\emph{phansānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{phãsānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to ensnare\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{spāśáyati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to be bound\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13814).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phansānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phansānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum ne jhūṭ kahā to mujhe bhī phansāo ge.} — If you tell a lie, you will drag me into trouble too.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a hardship, then the Urdu for a change, then say \emph{phansānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پھنسانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To land in trouble; to trap\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
